headword: {宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}
gloss: evening star; Venus (in the evening sky)

definitions.gloss: evening star; Venus (in the evening sky)
definitions.explanation: The planet Venus when visible in the western sky after sunset. A poetic and traditional Japanese name for the bright planet that appears in the early evening.

examples.japanese: {宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}が{輝|かがや}いている。
{西|にし}の{空|そら}に{宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: I could see the evening star in the western sky.

examples.japanese: {宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}と{明|あ}けの{明星|みょうじょう}は{同|おな}じ{金星|きんせい}だと{知|し}って{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised to learn that the evening star and the morning star are the same planet Venus.

notes:
A classical and literary name for Venus when it appears in the evening sky. The word {宵|よい} means 'early evening' and {明星|みょうじょう} means 'bright star.' Venus is the brightest object in the night sky after the moon, making it easily identifiable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}が{輝|かがや}く: the evening star shines
- {宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}が{見|み}える: the evening star is visible

RELATED WORDS:
- {明|あ}けの{明星|みょうじょう}: morning star — Venus when visible before sunrise
- {金星|きんせい}: Venus — the astronomical name
- {一番星|いちばんぼし}: the first star visible in the evening — often Venus
- {宵|よい}: early evening — the period just after sunset

cross_references.label: the first star visible in the evening
